steps.content: The idea says yesterday's fall predicts a bounce, so I want yesterday's return with a minus sign outside: a bigger fall gives a bigger factor value. I'll start with the simplest form — minus one times the one-day return — to see how much of it survives after the short-term reversal style is removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The one-day return is exactly the short-term reversal style that gets subtracted out, so its incremental IC is zero. To keep the same idea but measure yesterday's fall in a way that isn't a single day's return, I'll use the distance from yesterday's close to the low of the past two days — a bigger drop means more distance, and it is not a pure one-day return.
error: ts_min(): window must be a positive integer
The window for ts_min has to be a positive integer; I'll fix that by taking the minimum over two days of each day's low first, then dividing close by that minimum.
error: invalid expression syntax: unmatched ')'

That had a stray parenthesis — the lag should go outside the whole expression, not inside it. I'll write it properly: minus one times (close divided by the minimum low of the last two days), lagged one day so it is yesterday's fall.
error: invalid expression syntax: unmatched ')'

Same issue again — the lag must be outside the ts_min call. I'll write it as one expression: close divided by the minimum low of the last two days, with the minus sign outside, then a one-day lag so it refers to yesterday's fall.
error: invalid expression syntax: unmatched ')'

I keep making the same mistake — the lag must be applied after the whole expression, not inside the ts_min call. One more attempt in the right form: minus one times the distance from yesterday's close to the low of the past two days.

The idea is short-term reversal: yesterday's return, with the sign flipped so a big fall gives a high factor value. I'll start with the simplest form — minus one times yesterday's close-to-close return — to see how much of it survives after the known reversal style is removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw one-day return is fully absorbed by the short-term reversal style, so the incremental part is zero. I'll keep the same idea but measure the fall as the distance from yesterday's high down to the close — a one-day drop that didn't reach the high — which is still a fall but not the same quantity as close-to-close return.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0300
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0143 (t = 5.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0263, 2023 +0.0122, 2024 +0.0103

Measuring the fall as the drop from the high to the close keeps most of it after the known styles are removed (+0.0143, t = 5.7) and is positive in all three periods. Since the idea is specifically about yesterday's fall, I'll now test the same measure over only yesterday's session rather than a full day's return, to see whether the one-day version is stronger.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0328
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0118 (t = 4.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0129, 2023 +0.0135, 2024 +0.0095

Lagging it to one day drops it to +0.0118, so the fall measured yesterday's full session is the better form. One last check: ranking each day's fall across coins before averaging over a few days, which should cut single-day noise while still following the same idea.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0480
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0210 (t = 8.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0304, 2023 +0.0201, 2024 +0.0172

Ranking the fall across coins before averaging lifted it to +0.0210 with t = 8.4 and the same sign in every period, so I'll stop here rather than spend another test on marginal tuning.

What I found: the idea holds on this history, but only when the fall is measured as the distance from yesterday's high down to the close — that quantity is not the same as close-to-close return, which is entirely absorbed by the known short-term reversal style. Measuring it over yesterday's full session was better than over just one day, and ranking each day's fall across coins before averaging over five days helped a lot. The factor keeps the direction the idea states: coins that fell a lot yesterday get a high value.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('close')) - 1).sec_rank().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about dollar volume, so I measure it as quote_volume (USDT traded) and put the negative sign outside because the factor should rise when dollar volume falls. First test: the simplest version, a short 5-day mean of negative log dollar volume.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0440
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0115, 2023 +0.0085, 2024 +0.0035

A 5-day mean works (incremental IC +0.0071, t = 5.6), but 2024 is weak (+0.0035). Since a single day's quote volume can be noisy, I'll test the same idea with a 20-day median instead of a mean to see whether a robust measure of low dollar volume is stronger.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0277
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0017 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0006, 2023 -0.0017, 2024 -0.0029

The 20-day median is worse (−0.0017, t = −2.0), so a long median loses the signal rather than capturing it. That tells me the effect lives in recent, not persistent, dollar-volume low, so I'll shorten the window to 10 days and keep the mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0414
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0070, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0028

The 10-day mean is also weaker (+0.0053 vs +0.0071), so shortening the window hurt; the 5-day mean stays the best. One last check: using a median at the same 5-day window to see whether robustness improves it without changing the window length.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0383
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 3.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0079, 2023 +0.0047, 2024 +0.0021

The 5-day median is worse (+0.0043, t = 3.6), so the mean at that window is the best of the four, and I stop here.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history — coins trading little in dollar terms do better afterwards, with a rank IC of +0.044, and the sign is consistent across all three periods. Most of that signal is in the known liquidity style, so the incremental part is only +0.0071 (t = 5.6), meaning the effect is small and mostly explained by how much money a coin is moving around. Shorter windows (10 days) and more robust measurements (medians) both lost ground, so the useful part is a recent average of dollar volume, not its long-run level.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).ln()</factor>

The idea says low dollar-volume is bullish, so the factor should be the negative of a dollar-volume measure. I'll start with the simplest form: minus one-day quote volume averaged over a short window, using USDT-quoted volume so it's comparable across coins without any price scaling.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0440
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0115, 2023 +0.0085, 2024 +0.0035

A 5-day mean of dollar volume gives a decent absolute IC but only +0.0071 after style removal, because a single day's volume spike dominates a short mean. Next I'll smooth over a longer window (10 days) to see whether a steadier measure is stronger in the incremental part.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0414
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0070, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0028

The 10-day mean is worse (+0.0053), so a longer smoothing doesn't help — the signal lives in recent volume. Since a single day's volume spike dominates, I'll try a median over the same 5-day window to see whether ignoring a few extreme days keeps the incremental IC up while staying closer to the idea's "very little" wording.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0383
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 3.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0079, 2023 +0.0047, 2024 +0.0021

The median is worse (+0.0043), so smoothing away extreme days isn't the answer. One last form worth checking: a long 60-day average of dollar volume, which asks "has this coin traded little over the last quarter" rather than "what happened yesterday."

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0299
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0015 (t = 2.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0022, 2023 +0.0015, 2024 +0.0012

The 60-day average is the weakest of the four (+0.0015), so the signal is genuinely recent rather than a persistent trait. That's two tests in a row that failed to improve on my best (+0.0071), so I'll stop here and hand in the 5-day mean of dollar volume with a negative sign.

What I found: coins that traded little in dollar terms do outperform over the next day — the plainest version, minus one-day quote volume averaged over five days, has rank IC +0.044 and incremental IC +0.0071 (t = 5.6), positive in all three sub-periods (+0.0115, +0.0085, +0.0035). The effect is real but small, and it is largely explained by the short-term reversal style that gets removed: smoothing the volume over longer windows or ignoring extreme days both diluted it. The idea holds on this history, but the edge is modest and lives in the last few days.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says low dollar-volume is bullish, so the factor should fall as quote_volume rises. I'll start with the simplest form: negative of the 20-day average dollar volume, using `quote_volume` (in USDT) so it's comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The 20-day mean is essentially flat once liquidity is removed (incremental IC 0.0011), so a single-day estimate of volume is too noisy. I'll replace it with a 20-day median of dollar volume, which ignores a few extreme volume spikes.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0277
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0017 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0006, 2023 -0.0017, 2024 -0.0029

The median is no better (−0.0017) and less stable across periods, so the median doesn't help. Since a short window of volume is noisy, I'll lengthen the window to 60 days while keeping the same negative sign.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0299
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0015 (t = 2.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0022, 2023 +0.0015, 2024 +0.0012

The 60-day mean gives rank IC +0.0299 but still only +0.0015 after style removal, so the signal is entirely within the liquidity style. One last check: I'll measure the same idea in a different way — where each coin's recent dollar volume sits inside its own 60-day range — which is scale-free and less tied to a single average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

The rank-inside-own-range version works much better: +0.0139 incremental (t = 5.1) with all three periods positive, so the signal really is about where a coin's dollar volume sits in its own recent range, not about the level of dollar volume. Since the idea names dollar volume specifically, I'll hand in that form rather than the simpler level-of-volume version that scored 0.0015.

What I found: measuring dollar volume as a level average over 20 or 60 days gives almost nothing once liquidity is removed (+0.0011 and +0.0015), because a single-day dollar volume level is exactly what the liquidity style already captures. Only by comparing a coin's recent dollar volume to its own 60-day range does the idea survive, and that is what I'm submitting.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=60, min_periods=48)</factor>

The idea says dollar-volume is bearish, so I'll measure it as negative log `quote_volume` (log of USDT volume, so it's comparable across coins of very different size) and average it over a short window. First test: a 5-day mean of the negative log.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0412
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0057 (t = 4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0097, 2023 +0.0065, 2024 +0.0028

The 5-day mean is mostly the known liquidity style (0.004 incremental, t = 4.9) — a single day's volume spike dominates. So I'll shorten the window to 3 days to make it less dominated by one-off volume spikes.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0428
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0064 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0108, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0034

Shortening to 3 days gave +0.0064 versus +0.0057 — a gain of only 0.0007, well inside noise, and the 2024 slice is weaker. Since the idea is about unusual quietness, I'll test a median instead of a mean over the same 3 days to suppress those one-off spikes.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0413
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0059 (t = 4.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0089, 2023 +0.0060, 2024 +0.0042

The median gave +0.0059, again only 0.0005 better than the 3-day mean — two tests in a row that failed to clear the 0.002 bar, so I'll stop here and hand in the simpler form.

What I found: the idea holds in raw form — low dollar volume does predict better forward returns (+0.0412 rank IC), but almost all of that is the known liquidity style: after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum only +0.0057 survives (t = 4.9). Shortening the window to 3 days and switching to a median did not add anything meaningful, so this factor is essentially the liquidity style with a very short averaging window. Direction is kept as the idea states it: the factor is negative log dollar volume, so quiet coins score high.

The idea says a large fall yesterday predicts a bounce, so the factor should rise when yesterday's return is negative. I'll start with the simplest form: minus yesterday's return, with no smoothing.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw one-day return carries zero incremental IC because a single day's return is exactly the short-term reversal style that's already stripped out. So I'll keep the same idea but express yesterday's fall as the size of the move relative to that coin's own recent volatility — a short-term-return-normalized version of "fell a lot".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0187
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0003 (t = -0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0003, 2023 +0.0001, 2024 -0.0011

Volatility scaling still gives essentially zero, because a single day's return is still the one-day return that gets removed. Next I'll measure the fall as the distance from yesterday's close back down to the low of the past two days, which is the shape of a bounce rather than the endpoint return — a single-day endpoint move shouldn't dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0149
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0008 (t = -0.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 -0.0008, 2024 -0.0012

All three forms of yesterday's fall have incremental IC near zero, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history. What I found: the idea holds in raw rank IC (+0.0175 for the simple −1 × yesterday's return), but once short-term reversal and momentum are removed, nothing of it is left — yesterday's return is exactly what gets subtracted out. Measuring the fall as a move relative to the coin's own recent volatility, or as the distance from yesterday's close down to the two-day low, does not rescue it either. So on this history the bounce is mostly short-term reversal, and I keep the direction the idea states.

The raw one-day return gives exactly zero incremental IC because a single day's return is fully absorbed by the short-term reversal style. So I'll keep the same idea (yesterday's return, negative) but average it over a few days to damp single-day noise.

Averaging over three days lifts incremental IC to +0.0078 with t = 3.5, and all three periods now point the same way. Next I'll check whether a longer average (five days) captures the bounce better, since the bounce is really about the day before yesterday.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0004

Five days drops it to +0.0003 — the bounce is short-lived, so averaging over more days washes it out. One last check: a one-day average with a short EMA to see whether smoothing the recent bounce adds anything without diluting it.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

A one-day EMA is exactly the same as the raw one-day return (+0.0000), so the extra smoothing adds nothing. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on +0.0078, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds in raw form only weakly — yesterday's fall is bullish, and rank IC is +0.0175 — but it is entirely explained by the short-term reversal style, so its incremental IC is exactly zero. Averaging the same bounce over three days keeps the idea's direction and gives +0.0078 incremental IC (t = 3.5), with all three periods positive. The bounce decays quickly: five days of averaging wipes it out (+0.0003), and a one-day EMA is no better than the raw return. I kept the negative sign on yesterday's return as the idea states.

The median is worse (+0.0043 versus +0.0071), so the effect is coming from typical dollar-volume rather than from a few extreme days. One last check: a slightly longer 10-day window of the same mean, to see whether a slower reading of "trades very little" holds up better than the 5-day one.

Coins that trade very little in dollar terms do tend to outperform next day, but only when the dollar-volume is measured over the last five days: +0.0071 incremental IC with t = 5.6, positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, though weaker in 2024. Medians and longer windows both did worse, so the effect lives in the typical dollar-volume rather than in a few extreme days.
